Saigonese bun cha and amazing crab rolls!
Dec 2024 • Friends
I went there by a recommendation with a friend who lived in HCMC as an expat. The place was packed during peaked hours so we made a booking in advance.

We ordered buncha with southern sauce and mixed of normal pork and bacon to try. Buncha was amazing, and gimmick of grilling pork and bacon added a nice touch to it. The vegetable side, typical in Vietnam, was huge and plenty. The sauce was yummy.

The crab roll is super big and tasty. It was served hot. I also tried their soda chan, soda with sugar and lime - was very refreshing.

We managed to get through this with limited English because the menu contained only buncha and rolls, not difficult to navigate. One of the best meal I have had in HCMC.

Good Bún Chả in Saigon
Aug 2024 • Couples
The Bún Chả tastes good. It is served with soft white vermicelli, mint leaves and other greens, two different fish sauces, and grilled marinated pork patties and bacon strips. What I love most is the Nem Cua Bể, crispy rolls with pork and crab meat. These are served on a griddle and go well with the Bún Chả. The only downside of this place is the tiny size of the restaurant. It can get rather uncomfortable when it is full of patrons. But I would recommend anyone who visits Ho Chi Minh City and would love to taste good Vietnamese food.

Crab egg rolls, grilled pork, rice noodles, vegetable soup broth, and greens!
Jan 2023
The title of my review tells you the ONLY things on the menu here except for drinks and one or two desserts. The only choices you have, really, are how many orders of the incredibly delicious crab roll, grilled pork, and lumps of cold, sticky rice noodles you want. 

I have eaten here many times and I've never been disappointed. When I have friends and relatives visiting in Ho Chi Minh City I always take them here and they always marvel at how delicious the food is. Unique and fantastic would be my two-word description. 

I'd recommend you get at least 2 - 3 crab rolls, 1 noodle order, and one order of grilled pork PER PERSON when you first order. That's because, after you've tasted the stuff you might want to order more -- and the wait for more will be long. Better to order up front! :)

Save yourself the trip: worst service and food in 4 weeks of vietnam!
Dec 2019 • Couples
CNN approved in 2012... they wouldn’t approve today. So save yourself the trip.

When walking in, it was crowded but little atmosphere, but who cares when you want to try the springroll... they had a sign that they increased their prices. 

They only serve bun cha and springroll (69.000 VDN). Drinks (for example softdrinks) were around 25.000 VDN. Bit expensive. 

We only wanted to try the springroll, but that was lost in translation. Service speaks practically no english. Unfriendly staff overall, walked away when we tried to call them to our table en we had to ask for our bill 4 times. I don’t mind asking several times, cause we are the non-vietnamese speaking guests; but it was overall chaos. 

So the food...
springroll-: 4/10. It was dry but the shrimp was okay. They cut it up with scissors in 4 pieces, so eating it is was challenging. There was no fish sauce or hot sauce. It was not worth the 69.000 VDN or the walk. 

Caution; they provide wet wipes, BUT YOU HAVE TO PAY for the wipes. In our 4 weeks in Vietnam we never had to pay for it... too bad it happend at a “restaurant” that sucked...

Grass roots modern Vietnamese
Oct 2019 • Friends
I met a friend and stopped here for lunch after an exhilarating motorbike ride through the city
This place is busy, definitely for young groups and families, noisy, and unapologetic for it
Wooden furniture, big tables, polished cement floors
There’s a terrace top which is where we were seated after a 5 minute wait downstairs 
I think it helped that my friend can speak Vietnamese as she said something to the staff and then we got our seats 
We had a sumptuous lunch of noodles with tangy fish sauce dressing, salad, pork and prawn dumplings (huge, 4 of them), pork mini bites and bacon on a burner (about 4 pieces of each) and green salad
Some iced water and iced tea to go with it
All promptly served, no waiting once seated
And so delicious, the style of food suits the setting and atmosphere 
Great for lunch or a group for dinner. To top it off, our bill was a grand $16 total

The Spring Roll as never before...
Sep 2018 • Family
It may well be that this is how they do spring rolls in Vietnam because this was the first time I ate them here. But wow! These guys have rewritten the rule book. Huge spring rolls wrapped in thick crisp mutlilayered pastry with a finely flavoured crab filling. About the size of a squashed tennis ball and the waiting staff will cut them up into four pieces. They account for half the menu the other half being some delicious pork. Served with cold rice noodles, a bowl of mixed raw greens and a sauce. Good fruit juices. Plus the atmosphere is kicking... Crowded to queing when we went on a Sunday evening but the staff seemed to have the waiting under control and we were seated in about 15 minutes. If ever a restaurant mirrored the character of a city, then this is it. Highly recommended experience but remember it is a sort of in your face kind of place so maybe not for the faint-hearted!

Okay, let me qualify this from the outset... If you have never had Bun Cha in Vietnam then you are missing a treat, but like many of their famous dishes such as Pho Bo, if you find 10 different restaurants with it on the menu then your will find 10 different ways that it is made and served, so much comes down to your own personal preference. Personally Bun Cha & Nem Cua (grilled pork in broth and crab spring rolls) is one of my absolute favourites and although the accompanying noodles are nearly always stone cold when served, many versions are served with a hot broth allowing you to warm each delicious mouthful of them as you dip them in. Not so here, cold noodle and cold broth and a few slices of pork that will also be cold by the time they are dipped into the bowl. Oh well, as I said, this isn't uncommon just not the way I like it myself. That is fair enough but the price is double that of many other places serving the same dish, and while around a 120vnd a head for your main, one crab roll side (albeit large) and a beer may not break the bank, for any budget traveller knowing that you can find the same or better (I will be posting a review of just such a place shortly, but shhhhh it is a secret :P) at half such the price then it comes down to other considerations. Like service and atmosphere...Now this is certainly a locally frequented place, but not in the same way that many of the tasty plastic stooled, one dish eateries many of you may see everywhere throughout Vietnam and HCMC are, no this is a place for locals who are upwardly mobile and are enjoying the ability to flash the cash a little bit, and this seems to come at the cost of politeness to many of the members of staff, who in fairness to counter this point seem to wander aimlessly not sure what table has ordered what and being quite abruptly shouted at. Neither party is entirely right in such situations but it doesn't make for a particularly enjoyable atmosphere as someone screams across your table for service and a lacklustre waiter arrives with your spring roll 15 mins after the rest of your order. The last point is that this is a Bun Cha and crab spring roll restaurant so don't expect to be able to order anything other than these dishes. My partner and I went knowing this but please don't think there is anything else on the menu or you will be disappointed. If you have never tried Bun Cha, are nearby and wanting to try and it's upmarket, trend-setter style is within your food budget and disposition give it a go but, if you already have a taste for this lovely dish and are counting pennies, just walk on past and find one of the other places for one of the more authentic and nicer toned places that really can be found.

Reading other reviews, there seem to be a running theme of accidentally running into this place. I was semi-exploring my hood (Dakao area of Q1), and there it was. Good tip from Noritaka1 about the two sauces.

Ordered both dishes. The Bun Cha came fairly quickly. The Nem Cau came a bit later. Basically half way through my Bun Cha.

The Bun Cha was good as I'd been searching for good ones in Saigon since I'd had the great one in Hanoi. By default they serve it with lighter of the fish sauce. You can ask for the thicker one.

The star of the show is definitely the Nem Cau (crab springroll). According to useful background on the menu, Quan Nem serves it Haiphon style. Haiphong is the norther city that's famous for their variety of seafood including the Nem Cua.

It came out in square shape. Each order = 1 square. The waitress/waiter will cut it into four pieces at the table for you. Each piece is equal to about 2 pieces of regularly size Vietnamese roll. 

So how does it taste? Damn good!

The filling was generous. Packed with all the goodness. The skin is so light, crispy, and fluffy it melts in your mouth. First this happens for me with fried Vietnamese spring roll.

I always prefer rice paper as it's lighter than egg-roll paper. Don't know what kind of paper they use here but the result is unmatched. 

Got a sour sop drink to go along with it too. 

Hope to see more good review on Quan Nem so this place gets pushed up even more.

The whole cost me around $5-$6 USD (1 order of Bun Cha, 1 order of Nem Cau, 1 sour sop smoothie). Unbeatable value.

In all, a great great and unexpected experience!

TIPS: 
1. Order both dishes esp if you're hungry. The Nem Cau will come around half way mark as you work your way through the Bun Cha. 
2. Ask for two fish sauces for variety as they by default serve just one. Ask for both Northern/Southern style (Nuoc Man Bac hoac Nuoc Mam Nam) [credit to noritaka1 for this]
